en: In a vacuum, a heavy bowling ball and a light feather fall at the exact same rate due to gravity.
Static friction prevents a parked jeepney from sliding down a steep hill even before its wheels start moving.
Magnets strongly attract ferromagnetic metals like nickel and cobalt, not just iron.
A pulley system makes lifting a heavy sack of rice easier by reducing the required force, not the total work.
Light takes about eight minutes to travel from the Sun to the Earth, proving it does not travel instantly.
Sound cannot travel through the vacuum of outer space because it requires a physical medium like air to vibrate.
An ice cube cools your warm juice by absorbing heat energy from the liquid, rather than releasing coldness.
A flashlight bulb transforms electrical energy into light and heat, but the electrical current itself is never consumed.
When a rolling toy car stops, its kinetic energy is transformed into heat and sound, not destroyed.
Pushing a box up a wooden ramp requires less lifting force than carrying it straight up the stairs.
Astronauts float on the International Space Station because they are in continuous freefall, not because space has zero gravity.
If you break a bar magnet in half, each new piece will still possess both a north and south pole.
